_comment: Recorded end-to-end accuracy per architecture. tests/test_accuracy.py fails
when a measured rate exceeds `error_rate_pct + tolerance_pct`, which is what
makes kernel and frontend work safe to merge: a parity suite cannot catch a
feature-convention bug, because it feeds identical features to both sides and
the error cancels. The audio_scale defect shipped through exactly that gap.
These numbers are for REGRESSION DETECTION, not publication. LJSpeech is
out-of-domain for all of them, and the subset is 200 utterances. Do not
quote them as OASR's WER, and do not read them as a ranking either: the
checkpoints differ in size, training data and license.
To re-record after a deliberate accuracy change, run the command in
`recorded_with` for each entry and update `error_rate_pct` in the same commit
as the change, with the reason in the commit message.
Tolerance sizing: measured bit-stable across 3 consecutive runs and across
max_batch_size 1/8/16/32 (identical error counts), so 0.3 absolute is slack
for a different GPU or torch build, not for run-to-run noise.
Recorded 2026-08-11, the first WER this architecture has ever had: it was
the one registered architecture with no real checkpoint, so greedy decode,
beam search and streaming had only run on random weights.
icefall zipformer/2023-05-15 (Zipformer2 medium + stateless predictor +
joiner). Upstream reports 2.27 / 5.10 on LibriSpeech test-clean/test-other;
3.23 here is out-of-domain LJSpeech, so the two are not comparable except
as a sanity bound. Loading needs `load_architecture` because an icefall
pruned-RNNT dir sniffs as `zipformer` and the converter is explicit-only.
NOT batch-invariant, unlike the offline rows above, and the reason is
structural rather than reduction order: max_batch_size 1 gives 3.76%
(62S 51D 15I) against 3.23% at 8 and 16, and 3.26% at 32. The 20 extra
deletions at batch 1 are trailing words: a padded batch gives every
utterance right-padding up to the batch maximum, which the transducer
flushes remaining symbols on, while a batch of one gets almost none. Same
mechanism the nemotron_streaming row documents in the other direction. That
is worth fixing in the offline flush rather than tolerating, so this entry
is pinned at 16 and the spread is recorded here instead of widening the
tolerance.
beam_size=1 is token-identical to greedy on all 200 utterances (the gate);
beam_size=4 gives 3.03% (62S 26D 15I).
Recorded 2026-08-05. Bit-stable across max_batch_size 1/8/16/32 —
identical error counts — which is the property that had to be earned:
the first measurement was 2.70% at bs16 and 2.62% at bs1, and the
difference was a fused-attention defect on -inf mask floors, not noise
(see oasr/models/nemotron/encoder.py::MASK_FLOOR). At the time float32
gave 2.59% against fp16's 2.62, one fewer deletion.
Decoded with the checkpoint's own default language prompt (slot 101,
'auto'); pinning en-US does not change this manifest's rate.
Re-recorded 2026-08-20 at 2.59 (was 2.62), one fewer deletion, when the
predictor's LSTM moved from nn.LSTM to oasr.layers.LSTM. Not noise and
not a defect: the fused kernel accumulates both gate dot products in
fp32 (float accum[4] + fmaf) where cuDNN's fp16 path does not, so fp16
now lands on the fp32 rate recorded above. Measured twice, before and
after the finalizer/cell-ring changes in the same branch, with
identical error counts (69S 8D 11I) all four times — so the 0.03 is the
accumulation precision and nothing else.
Recorded 2026-08-05. The STREAMING service mode on the same manifest and
the same denominator as the offline `nemotron` row above, so the two are
directly comparable — which is the point of gating it: a streaming
regression that a parity test structurally cannot see (a cache that
silently resets, a flush that truncates the last word) lands here as
deletions.
Streaming is *better* than offline (2.44 vs 2.62; 66S 6D vs 69S 9D). The
extra trailing silence a closed stream is padded with gives the transducer
more frames to flush on than offline's single right-pad frame does.
Spread: 2.41-2.53 over max_batch_size 1/8/16/32 and 2.44-2.50 over
chunk_size 4/8/16/32, with deletions stable at 5-7. float32 at bs8 gives
2.41 with identical counts to fp16, so the spread is batched-kernel
reduction order at wider batches, not precision — the same property the
stateful backend's batching has. It is NOT the batch invariance the
offline rows have, and that is expected: the offline forward is one
padded batch, a streaming step is a cohort whose width changes as streams
join and finish.
Two defects had to be fixed to get here, both in shared streaming code and
both invisible offline: the closing silence pad left 1..window frames of
flush depending on utterance length (42 deletions at chunk_size 4), and a
CUDA-graph *capture* invalidates an earlier replay's output buffer, not
just a later replay at the same key (5 of 40 utterances lost their
trailing words). See .artifacts/kernel_coverage.md 12a.
Re-recorded 2026-08-20 at 2.41 (was 2.44), one fewer deletion, for the
same reason as the offline row above: the fused LSTM predictor
accumulates its gates in fp32. See that entry.
Recorded 2026-08-16 — the first WER the `llm` family has ever had, and
the reason it now has one: it is the family whose decode path H11
rewrote (per-row KV offsets, group merging, paged decoder KV, decoder
step CUDA graphs), and every test covering that path compared a step to
a step. A graph that captures something it should not returns a
plausible transcript, not a crash, so a tensor oracle is exactly the
instrument that cannot see it. The nemotron_streaming row above records
one that got through that way.
The three storage/graph arms are byte-identical over all 200
utterances: dense, kv_storage=paged, and kv_storage=paged +
step_graphs=1 produce the same transcript for every id, so this rate is
the same number whichever the engine defaults to.
`prompt` is pinned in the entry rather than inherited. This is the
*Instruct* checkpoint, and the shipped default is the official Qwen2-
Audio ASR prompt ('Detect the language and recognize the speech.'),
which the Instruct variant answers in prose — 76.56% on the first 8
utterances, almost all of it insertions like 'the language in the
speech is english and the transcription is ...'. That measures prompt
following, not recognition, and it would bury a real regression. A
prompt change is a WER change with no defect behind it, so it belongs
in the entry with the rest of the decode configuration.
bfloat16, unlike every row above, because the checkpoint declares it
(text_config.torch_dtype); fp16 is not what this model is served as.
Read 5.58 as a detector, not as a speech-recognition number. The
insertions are largely a surviving 'the transcription is' preamble, and
14 of the 50 deletions are one utterance (LJ001-0119) answered in
Chinese. Both are the LLM being an LLM. What the row catches is the
rate *moving*.
entries.recorded_with: python benchmarks/bench_accuracy.py --ckpt-dir $ASSET --manifest benchmarks/manifests/ljspeech_200.jsonl --audio-root $WAV_DIR --dtype bfloat16 --decode-option 'prompt=Transcribe the audio into text. Output only the transcription, with no extra words.'

decode_options.prompt: Transcribe the audio into text. Output only the transcription, with no extra words.
